P1.evidence: Setter notes acknowledged only in passing ('you already had a conversation with Kim... you already gave me some idea from where you're at the moment'). Frame was three-part, not four - 'where you're at, specifically where you want to go. Also, if we can actually help you bridge that gap' - with no 'what you need' element. Agreement was sought with a tacked-on 'okay?' rather than a clean 'Does that work?'. Open question ran verbatim: 'what can we potentially specifically help you with, Frank?'

P2.evidence: Injuries were probed properly and specifically - 'you mentioned blow out your back again. So from what I hear, you've already blown out your back once. Is that correct?' and a follow-up on whether the shoulder hurts at rest or only under load. But age (49), height, weight and self-employment were all volunteered, never asked. Cancer, Lyme, mould and autoimmune history were volunteered inside a goals answer and the rep never asked a health-conditions question. Nutrition and eating window were asked well. Sleep was never raised at all in a prospect who described autoimmune fatigue and wanting 'to sleep all the time'.

P3.evidence: Strongest phase. 'when it comes to your goals, sort of paint that for me', an explicit mobility question, and 'Is there something I would like to be able to do if I was in better shape?' which surfaced the Tough Mudder answer. Drove to the son and named it - 'being a role model, it sounds like' - after Frank volunteered 'he's never seen me really healthy'. The scripted 'outside of the physical, what's actually driving this' bridge was replaced with a softer 'what would be that feeling for you', and the reflect-back at 00:19:07 recited a physical checklist (weight, clothes, mobility) instead of the 'this isn't really about the weight, it's about being there for your son' reframe that was sitting right there.

P4.evidence: Frank volunteered a rich history - trainers since the early 2000s, some with medical backgrounds, who 'didn't really understand the complexity of what was going on in my body' - and the rep never asked what happened with any of them or why it did not stick. The gap did get named, but by the prospect and late: 'it's not a structured plan, it's not, it's not targeted enough... I've been just sort of flying blind for a while'. The nearest run at P4f was 'there's also people who just try to figure it out all by themselves online. What was the purpose of booking this meeting?'

P5.evidence: Ran the frame: 'how do you feel like that would be in the next year or two years or so if it constantly stays at like that same level?' and then 'is that something that you would even want to settle for that you just fall back into?', getting 'absolutely not'. Never asked 'why not' - Frank supplied the answer himself ('I'm going to be 50 this year... I'm going to have a very painful old age'). The line in the sand was asserted rather than asked: 'Sounds like you're ready personally to actually make sure you are locked in.'

P6.evidence: P6a was asked and, when Frank said 'I'm sorry, could you repeat the question?', asked again in cleaner form - good discipline. But the answer was 'I think so', which is not a clear yes, and the rep went straight into the presentation anyway. P6b was never asked. Later, at 00:45:44, he got 'Yeah, it could be' and correctly noticed - 'Doesn't sound all too certain' - but pressed on to price rather than returning to Phase 5 as the script requires.

P11.evidence: Price was quoted at 00:47:04 with the prospect already asking to wrap up, and the answer was 'I'll think about it'. No agreement was reached, so no payment, Trevor onboarding call, agreement email or Skool step could be reached.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger was explicit: 'Yeah, I'll think about it.' The rep ran the isolation move - 'Outside of having to think about it, do you feel like this is something I see myself doing? Or is it only the aspect of choosing this one or the other one?' - and started on the decision criteria ('what sort of the checklist that you have for yourself?'). None of the harder moves ran: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here'. The prospect terminated the play: 'we're kind of talking about the same things over and over again.'

Cost was named as a decision factor before price was even quoted - 'it all depends on timing and cost and everything as well' - and again in 'I often try to throw money at a problem.' After the 6K figure landed the rep never isolated finances, never asked 'finances aside, is there anything else keeping you from 100%', and ran none of the financial-picture questions. No payment plan was mentioned at any point.

'it all depends on timing and cost' triggered it. The rep did open with 'when it comes to timing aspect, well, what do you mean with that?' but the prospect redirected to his hard stop and the play was abandoned. None of the substantive moves - things never slow down, the longer you wait the harder it gets, the only thing you can control is right now - were run.

Doubt about the coach and the relationship: 'I don't know this person. I don't know what their relationship is going to be like, and I can't say that 100%.' The rep ran a gut-feeling isolate - 'you always have somewhat of a gut feeling, right?' - and got 'I'm interested', but ran none of the scripted OE moves (certainty question, bridge, plane, burned before).

SCRIPT GAP - active comparison shopping. 'I'm investigating a couple of other opportunities right now... I've got another person from the internet that I'm meeting with this week also.' There is no play in the playbook for a prospect running a live bake-off against other coaches, and the rep had nothing to reach for; he conceded the ground ('I'm definitely going to give you that room') and the call ended.

SCRIPT GAP - clinical fit. 'I know with kettlebells, there's a lot of pressing. There's a lot of overhead pressing. So I may need to go a little bit easy on that side.' From a prospect with an actively painful shoulder and an L4/L5 herniation, this is the medical-fit objection the playbook already acknowledges it has no play for. The rep answered with reassurance ('that's normal, especially in the beginning') rather than any screening or clearance step.

notes: Discovery on goals and consequence was genuinely good and the son thread was well worked, but the rep never asked a single past-attempts follow-up despite Frank handing him a decade of failed trainers, and never asked about sleep in a man describing autoimmune fatigue. The call-losing error is structural: he spent 47 of 49 minutes in discovery and presentation and quoted price with two minutes left against a stated hard stop, so no objection play had room to run. Coach him to timebox discovery and get to price by the 35-minute mark, and to treat 'I think so' / 'it could be' as a Phase 5 return, not a green light.
